---
**Found by inversion: the waitlist was supposed to be the cost gate. How does it become a cost hole?**

Sign-up is now open by design, so the create-organization endpoint is an unauthenticated-by-intent write path. Nothing in the plan caps it. One person can create unlimited organizations, and every new Google account that signs in is a Cognito monthly active user. The free tier is 10,000 MAU and then it is 0.015 per user, which is small until someone points a script at it.

Real Google accounts are a barrier, not a wall.

**Do:** one organization per person unless an operator lifts it, a rate limit on creation, and a CloudWatch alarm on Cognito monthly active users well below the free tier boundary so we learn about a flood from an alarm rather than an invoice.

**Note:** a waitlisted principal already costs only one DynamoDB read per request, so this is about the write path and the MAU count, not about serving them.
payload.title: Cap organization creation and alarm on Cognito users
